title: OpenAI /v1/chat: param mapping, sparse-stop support, and stream handshake stability
author: Ava Cheng
release_notes: Adds broader OpenAI /v1/chat compatibility: flexible param mapping, support for sparse stop sequences, stabilized streaming handshake around tool/function calls, and a new logprob envelope for per-token deltas. No behavioral breaking changes expected for existing Redwood API callers.
description: Context: Customers using /v1/chat compatibility reported two recurring issues: (1) sparse/heterogeneous stop sequences (arrays of strings and nulls, mixed length) were not consistently honoured across streaming vs non-streaming paths; (2) streaming tool/function-calls produced fragile boundaries that sometimes dropped final comma/role tokens and made downstream tool parsers fail. This PR standardizes param mapping (allowing more OpenAI-style aliases), implements a tolerant sparse-stop mapper, and introduces an explicit streaming handshake event for function/tool calls to ensure deterministic framing. Summary of changes, tests, and rollout notes are in this single description string to keep the PR page compact.
commits: a3f4b6c: api: add v1_chat param mapper (aliases for max_tokens, top_p, temperature, n)
b9d2e1f: runtime: sparse stop mapper - normalize arrays and remove empty/null entries
c4e7fa2: streaming: emit 'tool_call_start' handshake event and finalize 'tool_call_end' on completion
d172b98: compat: migrate logprob streaming envelope to per-token 'delta_logprobs' array and deprecate legacy 'running_logprobs'
e81ac9d: tests: unit + integration covering stop permutations and streaming handshake recovery
f2a0b44: docs: docs/site/openai-compatibility/v1-chat.md - examples and migration notes
discussion: Diego Marquez (reviewer): Can you add a short doc blurb about how nulls in stop arrays are handled? Some customers send [null, '\n'] and expect sane behavior.
Ava Cheng (author): Added normalization rules to stop_normalizer and a paragraph in docs. Null/empty entries are now removed and duplicates deduped while preserving ordering semantics where possible.
Priya Raman (reviewer): Streaming: what happens when a tool_call_start is emitted but the worker crashes before tool_call_end? We need a graceful timeout and fallback so callers don't hang.

Ava Cheng (author): Implemented a 30s handshake TTL in stream_framing; if tool_call_end isn't seen within TTL, runtime emits 'tool_call_timeout' and falls back to assistant finalization. Added integration test that simulates worker kill.
Owen Li (approver): Verified perf microbench; mapping layer adds ~0.1ms median overhead on hot path. CI integration + e2e stream tests passed locally. Approving.
